summary: Backend health + realtime-session verified against LIVE OpenAI: /api/health returns openai_key_configured=true, model=gpt-realtime-translate; POST /api/realtime-session returns 200 with value starting 'ek_', expires_at, and session.type=='translation' (no 'sk-' leak). Frontend E2E: pressing START correctly acquires mic (Fake Default Audio Input), requests /realtime-session (200 ek_...), creates SDP offer, and POSTs to https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/translations/calls — BUT that call returns HTTP 429 insufficient_quota: 'You have no credits remaining. Add credits to continue using the API at https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing/.' The frontend correctly surfaces this as an error banner ('Failed to connect to OpenAI Realtime (429). ...'), tears the PeerConnection down cleanly, restores the START button, and no permanent 'sk-' key ever appears in browser-visible responses. Because of the 429, the OpenAI status dot never reaches 'connected', the STOP button is not shown, the timer stays at 00:00:00, and no session.created event is captured. All backend/frontend code paths are correct; the failure is an OpenAI account credit issue on the configured OPENAI_API_KEY.

integration_issues.flow: WebRTC handshake to OpenAI Realtime Translations
integration_issues.issue: OpenAI /v1/realtime/translations/calls returns 429 insufficient_quota ('You have no credits remaining'). App handles it correctly (error banner + clean teardown), but session cannot establish. This is an OpenAI billing/account issue — the ephemeral secret is minted successfully server-side, so app code is not at fault.

action_items: Add OpenAI API credits (or use a key on an account with billing/quota) — the current OPENAI_API_KEY in /app/backend/.env is valid enough to mint ephemeral client_secrets but the org has zero credits, so /v1/realtime/translations/calls returns 429 insufficient_quota and the WebRTC session cannot establish. After topping up credits, retest and expect status-openai-dot='connected', stop-translation-button visible, timer counting, and session.created event in the events stream.
OPTIONAL: In backend server.py you may want to sanitize the raw OpenAI error body forwarded via HTTPException detail (currently the browser sees the full upstream JSON incl. billing URL).
OPTIONAL: CORSMiddleware is added after app.include_router — conventional order is before include_router.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py forwards raw upstream OpenAI error text to the client — fine for debug but consider sanitizing in production.
translationEngine.js correctly separates ephemeral minting (backend) from the SDP call (browser direct) and never sees the permanent key. Good.
translationEngine._connect creates the RTCPeerConnection AFTER awaiting getUserMedia and ephemeral fetch — if start is cancelled during those awaits there is no early-abort check; minor.
translationEngine._handleDrop recurses via _handleDrop after reconnect failure without incrementing/backing off further guard beyond MAX_RECONNECTS check — acceptable but could tighten.

rca of the issue: RCA: OpenAI /v1/realtime/translations/calls responds 429 with body {error.type: 'insufficient_quota', message: 'You have no credits remaining. Add credits...'}. Reproduction: (1) GET /api/health -> openai_key_configured=true; (2) POST /api/realtime-session -> 200 + ek_ ephemeral (proves the API key is valid for minting client_secrets); (3) Open '/', click START — mic active, ephemeral received, SDP offer posted, then 429 returned by OpenAI causing translationEngine to throw OPENAI_CONNECT:429 and tear down. Mitigation: add credits to the OpenAI organization associated with the configured OPENAI_API_KEY, or swap in a key from a funded account, then retest. No code fix required.
